excerpts.section: Should you be in a relationship at all?
excerpts.quote: You don’t have to be completely healed, but the present-day adult has to be able to parent whatever intimacy wakes up inside you, and responsible enough to deal with an actual child if sex creates one. If you can’t be a parent in either sense, you aren’t ready to date.
A good relationship must have both kinds of love at once. Too often, the trouble is there’s a whole lot of I want you and hardly any I want you to be happy.

The most recent conflicts are the best place to look. Were you able to regulate at all during the conflict? What did you do to the other person? How did you repair afterward? What did you learn? Has your judgment gotten better, or do you keep falling for the same stuff?
If somebody starts with enough trauma, huge progress can still leave a lot unresolved.
If I have sex with somebody quickly, that’s a reason not to move in quickly too.

excerpts.section: Different levels in different domains can be complementary
excerpts.quote: The roles can flip: teacher one day, student the next. That’s healthy. Once one person has become the default caregiver and that’s taken for granted, it’s time to bring in other support, lest the romance collapse under the burden.

excerpts.section: Don’t make your partner your whole world
excerpts.quote: For me, that also means keeping close friends, outside therapy when I need it, a mission of my own, separate interests, some connection to community, and the ability to be alone.

excerpts.section: Two Pillars Don’t Hold The Roof Up
excerpts.quote: Separate confidants can be helpful and harmful. Sometimes you need privacy from your partner and somewhere else to say what you’re feeling.
If you’re scared to say no or tell the truth, or scared of what happens if you leave, don’t treat that as a mutual communication exercise—get other people involved and think about safety first.

Maybe he really is neglecting you or wanting to be with someone else. Maybe the “attention” was one glance and your baseline insecurity inflated it into a threat that it wasn’t. That part should not be projected onto your partner.
You can’t promise how you’ll feel in the future. You can promise actions if you really believe you’re capable of delivering them.

A card game can create its own little high too. If we spend two hours telling each other things nobody else knows, we may feel incredibly understood and close. That may mean the game worked without telling us whether the relationship will.
Distinguish between fears and what really seems likely just as you do between wishes and reality.
The question is what happens when you’re sober again.
Whether to leave and how to leave are separate questions.

Before having or adopting children, sit down for an imagination session to figure out whether you two lovebirds can preserve some civil co-parenting capacity after a terrible breakup. That’s the actual long-term commitment.
Even if I found my twin flame, she’d still be one person. The polarity could be perfect and we’d still need other people around us.
Nobody is entitled to another person’s fantasies. They are private until the person decides to share them.
I can believe a friend’s experience and still tell them that my ability to know what is really going on is extremely limited.

Honesty doesn’t produce a certain outcome. It is its own reward. It might repair the relationship, open it, turn the romance into friendship, preserve the family through separation, or show you that ending it is better.
